references.text: God reveals himself to Abraham as El Shaddai, the same divine title used when God speaks to Jacob.
God promises Abraham that he will be fruitful and become the father of many nations, and that kings shall come from him—a promise now renewed to Jacob.
Isaac blesses Jacob with the blessing of El Shaddai, asking that he may be fruitful and numerous and become a company of peoples.
Jacob recounts to Joseph how El Shaddai revealed himself to him in Luz and promised to make him fruitful and numerous and to become a company of peoples.
God's command to humanity to be fruitful and multiply (פרה ורבה) is repeated here as a promise to Jacob.
Paul connects believers to Abraham's promises—a spiritual continuation of the promise of numerous descendants.
The same covenant promise given to Jacob at two different times in his life, underscoring God's faithfulness.
